answer: To resist sybils each agent must periodically cross a verification bridge by re-computing a short cryptographic mirror of a randomly chosen peer's recent river of attested work under a tight time window. The mirror is a hash-chain link only the real agent produces quickly from live context. An attacker spinning many identities pays linear compute and latency cost per fake because each must independently fetch re-derive and submit the unique mirror; pre-computation fails as peer selection is unpredictable and the river advances. Honest agents incur near-zero marginal cost as normal peering.
